2022–2024 | team10 = [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] | highlights = * [[CBA International MVP]] (2021) * CBA All Import Player First Team (2021) * [[Chinese Basketball Association|CBA]] All-Star (2017) * [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] ({{nbay|2011|end}}) * Third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] – [[Associated Press|AP]] ([[2011 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2011]]) * First-team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] (2011) }} '''MarShon Scitif Brooks''' (born January 26, 1989) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=6 }}, he plays at [[shooting guard]] and [[small forward]] positions. Originally drafted by the [[Boston Celtics]] with the 25th pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]], he was immediately traded to the [[New Jersey Nets]]. ==Early life== Brooks was born in [[Long Branch, New Jersey]], and lived there until he was six years old, when his family moved to [[Stone Mountain, Georgia]]. He attended [[Tucker High School]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nj.com/nets/index.ssf/2011/06/marshon_brooks_is_happy_to_pla.html/|title=MarShon Brooks is happy to play for Nets, return to his New Jersey roots|work=[[New Jersey On-Line|NJ.com]]|date=June 27, 2011|access-date=June 28, 2011}} Considered a three-star recruit by [[247Sports.com]], Brooks was listed as the No. 126 shooting guard and the No. 521 player in the nation in 2007.[https://247sports.com/Player/Marshon-Brooks-63618/?Institution=9595 MarShon Brooks Recruiting Profile] ==College career== Brooks played collegiate basketball in the [[Big East Conference]] for the [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence Friars]].{{cite web|url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2011/02/23/big-easts-never-seen-a-game-like-marshon-brooks-had/|title=Big East's never seen a game like Marshon Brooks had|website=NBC Sports|date=February 23, 2011|access-date=December 31, 2021|first=Quinlan|last=Tess}} Brooks saw little playing time his freshman (2007–2008) and sophomore (2008–2009) seasons. Brooks began to become a major contributor for the Friars in his junior season ([[2009–10 Providence Friars men's basketball team|2009–2010]]). He averaged 14.2 points a game, shooting 46.7% from the field. Brooks posted 20 points or more in several games, including a 24-point game on 8-of-10 shooting against [[Vermont]] on November 24, 2009, a game in which he also picked up five steals. He recorded 25 points and five rebounds on January 23, 2010, against [[South Florida Bulls men's basketball|South Florida]]. As a senior in [[2010–11 Providence Friars men's basketball team|2010–2011]], Brooks averaged 24.6 points per game, first in the Big East. Besides leading his team in scoring and rebounding, he was second in Division I in scoring. He was named to the 30-player national midseason watchlist and was one of 20 national finalists for the 2011 [[John R. Wooden Award]]. On February 23, 2011, Brooks scored 52 points against [[2010–11 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|Notre Dame]], tying the school record held by [[Marvin Barnes]], and breaking the Big East record of 48 points in a game. He scored 35 points in the second half alone, 15 of them in the final 2:57, leading a comeback that would fall short as Notre Dame picked up the win, 94–93. Brooks scored his final points on a 3-point shot with two seconds remaining, leaving the Friars down a point. He hit 20-of-28 shots on the night. Fellow Friar [[Eric Murdock]] held the previous record of 48, set against [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]] in 1991. It was also Brooks' second 40-point game of the season; he had 43 in a loss at [[2010–11 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]] on February 5, 2011. He became only the third player in Providence history with two 40-point games in a season. On March 5, 2011, Brooks scored 28 points in a regular season-ending win over [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]], giving him 468 points on the Big East regular season. That broke the previous single-season conference mark of 462 points set by [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut]]'s [[Donyell Marshall]] in 1994. Brooks finished his college career with 1,629 points, ninth all-time for Providence. On March 28, 2011, he was named a third-team [[Associated Press]] [[2011 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]]. He was picked to the Fourth Team All-America by [[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]].{{cite news|first=Jeff |last=Goodman |url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711 |title=Goodman's 2010-11 All-America teams |work=[[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]] |publisher=Fox Sports Interactive Media |date=Mar 7, 2011 |access-date=June 21, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201123808/http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711 |archive-date=February 1, 2014 }} Brooks left Providence College with two months left in his senior year to focus on preparing for the [[2011 NBA draft]]. Brooks left school two classes short of obtaining his degree.{{cite web|title=PC's Brooks quits school to train for NBA Draft|url=http://www.projo.com/pc/content/sp_bkc_brooks_20_03-20-11_39N3M89_v3.1188feb.html}} His professional debut was delayed by the [[2011 NBA lockout]], so he took the time to return to Providence College to continue work on his degree and also work out with the Friars men's basketball team.[http://www.nypost.com/p/sports/nets/nets_brooks_handles_lockout_with_MN8Dqz2BpTDH9iE7ruvxKN Nets’ Brooks handles NBA lockout with ‘class’] ==Professional career== ===New Jersey/Brooklyn Nets (2011–2013)=== Brooks was drafted by the [[Boston Celtics]] with the 25th pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]], but the Celtics immediately traded Brooks to the [[New Jersey Nets]] for the Nets' 27th overall pick in the draft ([[JaJuan Johnson]]) and a second round pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]]. On February 8, 2012, Brooks was selected to participate in the 2012 [[BBVA Rising Stars Challenge]]. He was drafted by Team [[Charles Barkley|Chuck]]. On May 14, 2012, the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] announced that Brooks finished 10th in the Rookie of the Year voting with 4 total points. The winner was [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] guard [[Kyrie Irving]].{{cite web|title=Cavaliers' Kyrie Irving named Kia Rookie of the Year |url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/05/15/rookie-of-the-year-release/index.html |work=NBA.com |publisher=NBA |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120517101149/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/05/15/rookie-of-the-year-release/index.html |archive-date=2012-05-17 }} A few days later the NBA announced that Brooks had been named to the NBA All-Rookie Second Team. In 56 games Brooks averaged 12.6 points (3rd among rookies), 3.6 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 0.93 steals.{{cite web|title=MarShon Brooks named to NBA All-Rookie Second Team|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooks_named_to_nba_all_rookie_second_team_120522.html|work=NBA.com|publisher=NBA}} On November 9, 2012, Brooks sprained his left ankle during the team's morning shootaround.{{cite web|last=Mazzeo|first=Mike|title=MarShon Brooks sprains ankle|url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nba/story/_/id/8612013/marshon-brooks-brooklyn-nets-sits-hurt-ankle-gerald-wallace-again|work=[[ESPN]]|date=November 9, 2012 |publisher=ESPN}} Brooks would miss two games. In the beginning of the 2012–13 season, Brooks saw decreased playing time from Nets head coach [[Avery Johnson]]. Brooks admitted to having "confidence issues" early in the year. When P.J. Carlesimo became the team's coach, he gave Brooks more minutes. When Brooks was asked about Carlesimo he said, "I've got a lot more confidence. That's helped my game a lot."{{cite web|title=For MarShon Brooks, it's a confidence game|url=http://www.netsdaily.com/2013/3/9/4084156/for-marshon-brooks-its-a-confidence-game|work=netsdaily.com|date=March 9, 2013 |publisher=SBnation}} On April 3, 2013, in place of the injured [[Joe Johnson (basketball)|Joe Johnson]] against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], Brooks scored a career-high in 27 points on 12-of-16 shooting in a 113–95 win.{{cite web|title=MarShon Brooks scores career-high and D-Will dunks, as Nets blowout the Cavs, 113-95|url=http://www.netsdaily.com/2013/4/3/4180638/nets-cavaliers-scores-final-cavs-2013|work=netsdaliy.com|date=April 3, 2013 |publisher=SB nation|access-date=19 April 2013}} ===Boston Celtics (2013–2014)=== Brooks was traded back to the [[Boston Celtics]] on July 12, 2013, along with [[Keith Bogans]], [[Kris Humphries]], [[Gerald Wallace]], [[Kris Joseph]] and three first-round picks in a blockbuster deal that sent Celtics stars [[Kevin Garnett]], [[Paul Pierce]] and [[Jason Terry]] as well as prospect [[D. J. White|D.J. White]] to the Nets.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-complete-trade-brooklyn-nets|title=Celtics Complete Trade With Brooklyn Nets|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 12, 2013|access-date=July 14, 2013}} He was one of two players traded to the team that originally drafted them: Brooks was drafted by Boston in 2011 and Kris Joseph was drafted by Boston in the [[2012 NBA draft]]. On January 1, 2014, he was assigned to the [[Maine Red Claws]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15000 |title=Celtics assign MarShon Brooks to D-League |access-date=January 1, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140115145303/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15000 |archive-date=January 15, 2014 |url-status=dead }} On January 9, he was recalled by the Celtics.{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15054 |title=Celtics recall MarShon Brooks from D-League |access-date=January 10, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140111050708/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15054 |archive-date=January 11, 2014 |url-status=dead }} ===Golden State Warriors (2014)=== On January 15, 2014, a three-team trade was completed involving the Boston Celtics, the [[Golden State Warriors]], and the [[Miami Heat]]. The Celtics sent Brooks and [[Jordan Crawford]] to the Warriors. In exchange, the Celtics received [[Joel Anthony]], a protected future draft pick Philadelphia sent to Miami in an earlier trade, and a 2016 second-round draft pick from the Heat. The Heat also received [[Toney Douglas]] from the Warriors as part of the deal.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/crawford-brooks-trade-20140115|title=Warriors Acquire Jordan Crawford & MarShon Brooks From Boston Celtics|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=January 15, 2014|access-date=January 15, 2014}} On February 1, 2014, he was assigned to the Santa Cruz Warriors.[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-assign-bazemore-and-brooks-santa-cruz-warriors-nba-d-league Warriors Assign Bazemore and Brooks to Santa Cruz Warriors of NBA D-League] He was recalled the next day.[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/bazemore-brookes-recalled-from-santa-cruz-20140202 Warriors Recall Bazemore & Brooks From Santa Cruz Warriors of NBA D-League] On February 11, 2014, he was reassigned to Santa Cruz.[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/bazemore-brooks-kuzimic-assigned-20140211 Warriors Assign Bazemore, Brooks, and Kuzmic to Santa Cruz Warriors of NBA D-League] He was recalled the next day.[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/bazemore-brookes-kuzmic-recalled-from-santa-cruz-20140212 Warriors Recall Bazemore, Brooks & Kuzmic From Santa Cruz Of NBA D-League] ===Los Angeles Lakers (2014)=== On February 19, 2014, Brooks was traded along with [[Kent Bazemore]] from the [[Golden State Warriors]] to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in exchange for [[Steve Blake]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/140218bazemore_brooks_blake|title=Lakers Acquire Bazemore and Brooks|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Armani Milano (2014–2015)=== On August 8, 2014, Brooks signed a one-year deal with [[Olimpia Milano|Emporio Armani Milano]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian League]].{{cite news|title=Olimpia, ===Jiangsu Dragons (2015–2018)=== On August 5, 2015, Brooks signed with the [[Jiangsu Dragons]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA).{{cite web|title=MarShon Brooks Signs With Jiangsu In China|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/238955/MarShon-Brooks-Signs-With-Jiangsu-In-China|work=RealGM.com|date=August 5, 2015|access-date=August 5, 2015}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2018–2019)=== On March 27, 2018, the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] announced that they had signed Brooks to a 10-day contract.{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign MarShon Brooks to 10-day contract|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-marshon-brooks-to-10-day-contract-180327|date=March 27, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 27, 2018}} On April 6, 2018, Brooks signed a multi-year contract with the Grizzlies.{{Cite web |date=April 6, 2018 |title=Grizzlies sign MarShon Brooks to multi-year contract |url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-marshon-brooks-multi-year-contract-180406 |access-date=April 6, 2018 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} As part of a three-team trade with the [[Washington Wizards]], various news sources announced that MarShon Brooks would be traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]]. Reportedly, however, the Suns were led to believe that, rather than MarShon Brooks, they would receive [[Dillon Brooks]] in the trade deal. After a delay, it was finally reported that the Grizzlies refused to trade Dillon Brooks and ended their participation in the deal, which meant they would not receive [[Kelly Oubre Jr.]] from the Wizards.{{cite web|title=1 year later: The 'awkward' NBA trade that never happened due to last names|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2019/12/11/fallout-bizarre-trevor-ariza-dillon-marshon-brooks-trade|date=December 12, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=April 9, 2020}} On January 3, 2019, the Grizzlies traded Brooks, [[Wayne Selden Jr.]] and two future second round picks to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in exchange for [[Justin Holiday]].{{cite web |date=January 3, 2019 |title=Bulls deal Justin Holiday to Grizzlies for Marshon Brooks, Wayne Selden Jr. |url=http://www.nba.com/article/2019/01/03/release-bulls-complete-trade-grizzlies-justin-holiday |access-date=January 6, 2019 |work=NBA.com}}
